result.summary: Calls DisableNextWrite() at the start of each fuzz iteration across mempool and package evaluation fuzz targets (tx_pool, tx_pool_standard, tx_package_eval, ephemeral_package_eval, and validation_load_mempool). This prevents periodic chainstate flush-to-disk logic from executing unpredictably across inputs.
result.problem: Mempool acceptance calls FlushStateToDisk(PERIODIC), which checks a static m_next_write timer in chainstate. Because the timer carries over between fuzz iterations, an input's execution path depends on whichever inputs ran before it, causing non-deterministic coverage tracking and preventing crash inputs from reproducing in isolation.
evidence: Author measured periodic-write branch hits across shuffled replays on qa-assets using contrib/devtools/deterministic-fuzz-coverage, showing branch hits dropping from variable rates (e.g. 4 vs 17 in tx_pool) down to 0 in all five targets (PR description).
Fix follows the approach merged for process_message(s) and cmpctblock in PR #32822 (PR description).
result.scope_notes: A small 13-line patch across 3 fuzz target files; diff was omitted from context.
result.card: Calls DisableNextWrite at the start of each input in five mempool and package evaluation fuzz targets. Static chainstate previously leaked the periodic flush timer across fuzz iterations, causing non-deterministic execution paths and preventing crashes from reliably reproducing in isolation. The author measured using deterministic-fuzz-coverage on qa-assets that branch hit counts dropped from unpredictable values to zero across runs, mirroring the fix in merged PR #32822.

risk.why: Touches only fuzz testing harnesses, where an error could affect fuzz coverage or test execution without impacting production node behavior.
